attributes.morphology: dense to dispersed dendritic arm structure

evidence.quote: TiZrTaxNbMo RHEAs with a typical dendritic structure are composed of main BCC1 and minor BCC2 phases. With the decrease of the Ta content in the alloy, the volume fraction of the BCC1 phase gradually decreases, and the dendritic arm structure changes from a dense to dispersed condition.
The Ta0.7 alloy exhibit the highest plasticity, which is 34.8 %, while its yield strength is maintained at 1253 MPa.

The excellent mechanical properties of the alloys can be attributed to solid-solution strengthening and the formation of moderate amounts of interdendritic regions.
During the room-temperature compression process, the deformation mode of the alloy is always toward a dislocation slip, without the activation of other additional deformation mechanisms
The interaction between slip bands and dislocations formed during compression of the Ta0.7 alloy decreased its work hardening.
These results suggest that the superior strength and hardness of the alloy are caused by the solution-strengthening mechanism [49].

Elemental microsegregation was observed in the alloy, which is caused by non-equilibrium solidification. conflicts.description: Empirical solid-solution formation rules predict single-phase solid solution, but experiments show dual-phase BCC1+BCC2.

evidence.quote: Although the Ω values are greater than 1.1, and δ values are less than 6.6 %, it does not form a single-phase solid solution but a dual-phase solid solution, which is inconsistent with the empirical formula.

conflicts.description: Thermo-Calc equilibrium phase diagram predicts HCP phase at 500°C, but no HCP phase was observed experimentally.

evidence.quote: It is worth noting that the HCP phase appears in the phase diagram at 500 °C. However, no formation of this phase was observed by experimental characterization.
